Package neqsim.process.equipment.compressor

Class CompressorShaft

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.compressor.CompressorShaft
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class CompressorShaft extends Object implements Serializable
Groups several Compressor bodies that sit on ONE common shaft (driven by a single gas turbine or motor) so they must all turn at the SAME speed.

A multi-body compressor string (e.g. a recompression train BCL508-5 + BCL408 + BCL405/B on one gas-turbine shaft) cannot have each body solve its own speed independently: physically there is a single shaft speed, and only the string's final discharge pressure is a controlled target. The intermediate inter-body pressures therefore float — they are whatever each body produces at the common speed on its performance chart.

This class enforces that constraint. All member compressors are put in fixed-speed, chart-based mode (setSolveSpeed(false) + a common setSpeed) so each produces its discharge pressure from its chart at the shared speed. solveSpeed(neqsim.process.equipment.compressor.Compressor, double, java.lang.String, java.lang.Runnable) then does a one-variable false-position (Illinois) secant on the common speed until the reference (last) body's outlet pressure matches the target, re-solving the surrounding flowsheet between guesses via a caller-supplied callback.

Usage


 CompressorShaft shaft = new CompressorShaft("23-KA train");
 shaft.addCompressor(rc1); // 1st body
 shaft.addCompressor(rc2); // 2nd body
 shaft.addCompressor(rc3); // 3rd body (reference)
 shaft.setSpeedBounds(6000.0, 15000.0);
 shaft.setMaxShaftPower(24.0, "MW"); // or shaft.setTurbineDriver(gasTurbine)
 // re-run the whole flowsheet between speed guesses so inter-body streams update
 shaft.solveSpeed(rc3, 49.0, "bara", () -> process.run());
 double rpm = shaft.getSpeed();
 double util = shaft.getPowerUtilization(); // whole-string power vs the driver limit

Driver power limit

A common shaft has ONE driver, so the power limit belongs to the shaft rather than to any single body. Set it either explicitly with setMaxShaftPower(double, String), or from a driver model: setTurbineDriver(neqsim.process.equipment.powergeneration.GasTurbine) attaches a GasTurbine (the bodies become its driven loads, so its fuel gas and its own power utilization track the string duty, and its rated power limits the shaft) and setDriver(neqsim.process.equipment.compressor.CompressorDriver) attaches a CompressorDriver whose speed-dependent, ambient-derated curve is evaluated at the solved common speed. Gearbox losses are covered by setMechanicalEfficiency(double). getPowerUtilization() then reports the whole-string utilization and solveSpeed(neqsim.process.equipment.compressor.Compressor, double, java.lang.String, java.lang.Runnable) returns CompressorShaft.SolveStatus.OVER_POWER when the driver cannot deliver.

Gear ratios, idle members, ambient site rating and control targets

Members can sit behind a gearbox: addCompressor(Compressor, double) sets the member rpm per shaft rpm, so a body with ratio 1.2 runs at 1.2 x the common speed on its own chart. A member that is out of service (train off, parallel machine not running) is set idle with setMemberActive(Compressor, boolean): it is locked inactive, leaves the shaft power sum and the surge/stonewall checks, and a shaft with no active member reports CompressorShaft.SolveStatus.SHAFT_IDLE. setGasTurbineUnitDriver(GasTurbineUnit) makes a site-rated GasTurbineUnit (power versus ambient temperature, exhaust-temperature limit, fuel and exhaust heat) the driver, and setAmbientTemperature(double, String) moves its rating. solveSpeedToTarget(neqsim.process.equipment.compressor.Compressor, neqsim.process.equipment.compressor.CompressorShaft.ControlTarget, double, java.lang.String, java.lang.Runnable) controls the common speed from the discharge pressure, the suction pressure or the inlet flow of ONE controlling member, and getOperatingReport() lists, for every member, the speed, power, surge/stonewall margins and the recycle fraction that anti-surge would need. findMaxSpeedWithinPowerLimit(Runnable) gives the highest common speed the driver can hold, and DriverLimitedThroughputSolver the highest throughput.

    • setMemberActive

      public void setMemberActive(Compressor compressor, boolean active)
      Put a member in or out of service. An idle member (train off, parallel machine not running) is locked inactive so the flowsheet does not run it, and it is excluded from the shaft power, the speed application and the limit checks. The outlet stream of an idle compressor is not updated, so give an idle train a bypass line or zero flow in the flowsheet.
      Parameters:
      compressor - a member of this shaft
      active - true for in service, false for idle
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the compressor is not on the shaft

    • setDriverCurve

      public void setDriverCurve(DriverCurve curve)
      Attach a driver performance curve and take the speed band from it. For an electric motor with a variable-frequency drive this is the VFD range (minimum speed ratio to maximum speed ratio times the rated speed, including a cell bypass derating of the drive); for a fixed-speed motor it is the narrow band around the rated speed. The band is re-read at the start of every speed solve, so a change of the drive configuration is picked up. The curve also supplies the available shaft power at the common speed when no explicit limit, CompressorDriver or turbine is configured. The driver speed is the shaft speed: member speeds follow from the gear ratios.
      Parameters:
      curve - the driver performance curve, or null to detach it (the speed bounds stay as they are)

A motor without a performance model gives no speed band and no power limit.

    • solveSpeed

      public double solveSpeed(Compressor reference, double targetOutletPressure, String unit, Runnable processRun)
      Solve the single common shaft speed so that, after re-running the flowsheet, the reference body's outlet pressure equals the target. Uses a bracketed false-position (Illinois) secant on speed; higher speed gives higher head and therefore higher discharge pressure. Intermediate inter-body pressures float.
      Parameters:
      reference - the body whose outlet pressure is the controlled target (usually the last)
      targetOutletPressure - the required outlet pressure of the reference body
      unit - the pressure unit (e.g. "bara")
      processRun - a callback that re-solves the surrounding flowsheet (so inter-body streams, scrubbers and mixers update between speed guesses); may be null to just run the member compressors in series
      Returns:
      the solved common shaft speed in rpm

    • runAtFixedSpeed

      public void runAtFixedSpeed(double fixedShaftSpeed, Runnable processRun)
      Run every body at a locked, fixed shaft speed with NO speed iteration. This is the correct mode for a constant-speed driver (electric motor at line frequency, no variable-speed drive): the shaft cannot change rpm, so each body's discharge pressure floats off its chart at the fixed speed and any pressure spec must be met by anti-surge recycle, suction throttling or IGVs rather than by moving speed.
      Parameters:
      fixedShaftSpeed - the locked shaft speed in rpm
      processRun - a callback that re-solves the surrounding flowsheet, or null to run the member compressors in series

    • solveSpeedToTarget

      public double solveSpeedToTarget(Compressor controlling, CompressorShaft.ControlTarget target, double value, String unit, Runnable processRun)
      Solve the common speed so that one controlling member holds a target, with every other member floating on its chart at the same speed (times its gear ratio). This is the "controlling stage sets the speed" pattern: the member whose process flow and discharge pressure are fixed sets the shaft speed, the other members follow that speed and their surplus or deficit is read from getOperatingReport().

      CompressorShaft.ControlTarget.DISCHARGE_PRESSURE is solveSpeed(neqsim.process.equipment.compressor.Compressor, double, java.lang.String, java.lang.Runnable). For CompressorShaft.ControlTarget.SUCTION_PRESSURE and CompressorShaft.ControlTarget.INLET_FLOW the speed is bracketed on the speed bounds and found by false position; the direction of the response is not assumed, but the target must lie between the values at the two bounds, otherwise the status is CompressorShaft.SolveStatus.TARGET_OUT_OF_RANGE and the speed saturates at the closer bound. The result fields of CompressorShaft.SolveResult carry the controlled quantity in the given unit.

      Parameters:
      controlling - the controlling member (null selects the last active member)
      target - the quantity to hold
      value - the target value
      unit - pressure unit for the pressure targets, flow unit (e.g. "kg/hr", "m3/hr") for the flow target
      processRun - callback re-solving the flowsheet between speed guesses, or null
      Returns:
      the solved common shaft speed in rpm

    • findMaxSpeedWithinPowerLimit

      public double findMaxSpeedWithinPowerLimit(Runnable processRun)
      Find the highest common speed the driver can hold: the speed at which the required driver power equals the power available at the shaft ambient temperature (the speed bounds limit the search). Required power rises with speed, so a bisection on the power balance is used. The flowsheet is left at the returned speed. The result fields of CompressorShaft.SolveResult carry the available driver power (target) and the required driver power (achieved) in W.
      Parameters:
      processRun - callback re-solving the flowsheet between speed guesses, or null
      Returns:
      the highest feasible common speed in rpm, the minimum speed if even that overloads the driver, the maximum speed if the driver is never limiting or has no configured limit, and 0 for an idle shaft

    • applyRequiredRecycle

      public Map<String,Double> applyRequiredRecycle()
      Feed the recycle fraction each member needs (from getOperatingReport(), the distance of the operating point to the anti-surge control line) into the member's anti-surge: the built-in AntiSurge of the compressor is activated with the control line of the member (surge control factor from its surge control margin) and its valve position is set, and a registered recycle valve (setAntiSurgeValve(Compressor, ThrottlingValve) or setAntiSurgeController(neqsim.process.equipment.compressor.Compressor, neqsim.process.controllerdevice.AntiSurgeController)) is opened in proportion to the fraction. The built-in anti-surge acts inside the compressor run when the operating point is left of the surge line; between the surge line and the control line the recycle is carried by the valve opening and by the recycle power of the report. Re-run the flowsheet afterwards.

      The call is idempotent: the fractions are a function of the current operating point only, so repeating it without a change of that point gives the same state. A member that needs no recycle (or is idle) has its recycle set to zero, and a built-in anti-surge that this method switched on is switched off again; an anti-surge the user had activated stays active.

      Returns:
      applied recycle fraction per member name, in flow order

      private void applyRecycle(Compressor c, double f)

      f - the recycle fraction of the suction flow, in [0, 1)

    • evaluateFixedSpeedControl

      public List<FixedSpeedControlResult> evaluateFixedSpeedControl()
      Evaluate how every active member meets its required discharge pressure at the present, fixed shaft speed, using the member's chart: head deficit, recycle (through-flow, recycle fraction), throttling needed, and the shaft power and discharge temperature at the controlled operating point. This is the operating model of a constant-speed shaft, where the speed cannot be solved and the pressure set points are held by recycle or throttling.

      Set the pressure each stage must deliver with setMemberRequiredDischargePressure(neqsim.process.equipment.compressor.Compressor, double, java.lang.String), run the shaft at its fixed speed (runAtFixedSpeed(double, java.lang.Runnable)), then call this method. Idle members and members without a required pressure or a chart are returned as FixedSpeedControlResult.Status.NOT_EVALUATED. The flowsheet and the members are not changed. See CompressorFixedSpeedControl for the method and its assumptions.

      Returns:
      one result per member, in the order the members were added
